operation_details.item: The user prefers colloquial first-person phrasing in methods-section drafts instead of standard passive scholarly diction.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hey, I'm revising the methods section for the protein purification paper. I'm so done with the passive voice - I'm just going to say 'we did this' and 'we used that' to make it read like we actually did the work.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Ha, I get that. The passive voice can feel stiff. You're thinking of using first-person plural throughout? That's pretty casual for a methods section, but I can help you with that if you want.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yeah, exactly. I mean, who writes 'the solution was heated' when you can say 'we heated the solution'? It's more honest and reads better. I'm tired of the old-school scholarly diction.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Some journals do prefer that modern style. I can draft it that way. Should I also use contractions like 'we're' or 'didn't' to keep it really colloquial?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Sure, contractions are fine. Just keep it clear and direct. I think it makes the science more accessible. Plus, it's our work, so why pretend a disembodied hand did it?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Absolutely. I'll start rewriting the first paragraph using 'we' and a casual tone. I'll also check if the journal has any style guidelines that might conflict.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks. If they complain, I'll just say it's our voice. Honestly, I think the reviewers will appreciate the change. Let's do it.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Great. I'll send you a draft by the end of the day. Also, I remember you mentioned you like that style for grant proposals too - should I apply it there as well?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that In methods-section drafts, I want colloquial first-person phrasing such as 'I basically coded the transcripts by hand' instead of standard passive scholarly diction.
